blocks.text: One science is that which is of one genus of those things which are composed of first (principles), and are the parts or affections of these per se; but a science is different from another, whose principles are neither from the same things, nor one from the other. A token of this is when any one arrives at things indemonstrable, for it is necessary that they should be in the same genus with those that are demonstrated; it is also a sign of this when things demonstrated through them are in the same genus and are cognate.
